pieces.title: GemDroid
pieces.subtitle: Android × Gemini mascot
pieces.blurb: A friendly Android-style robot wearing a Gemini badge, modelled, textured, rigged and animated by one Gemini agent in a live Blender window.

pieces.title: MMSEV-AI
pieces.subtitle: Twelve-wheeled exploration rover
pieces.blurb: An exploration rover on six twin-wheel bogies, with a working animation: it drives on synchronised wheels, turns on the spot, sweeps its sensor turret and reaches out to take a sample.

viewer.note: The browser viewer plays one of the 38 separate animations at a time (Rover_Root, the drive); the recorded take shows the full coordinated animation.

pieces.title: Orbital inference node
pieces.subtitle: 3U CubeSat built to a written spec
pieces.blurb: A small satellite that carries an AI computer: deployable solar wings, radiators and an optical terminal, exported at real scale and checked against the spec's envelope.

pieces.title: AstroScout
pieces.subtitle: Rigged explorer robot
pieces.blurb: An early full run of the hybrid lane: a small explorer robot with a CRT-style helmet, rigged and given a looping wave. A warm-up made at 08:36–08:45 CET, before the hackathon window opened at 08:59; this run has no screen recording.

pieces.title: Platform 37 area study
pieces.subtitle: Four agents, one Blender
pieces.blurb: Four Gemini agents (modeler, props, look, camera) share one Blender through a turn queue. Asked for Platform 37, the design agent said it does not reliably know that name and modelled the railway-side landscraper at King's Cross instead. An unofficial study with no logos or signage.

facts.label: building + props
facts.source: output/director_render/scene_stats.json · includes the director's survey marker

honest: Wave 1 started with the viewport inside the building, so the change witness saw nothing and 15 edits were rolled back; an early camera session fixed the view and wave 2 resent them.
The look agent's switch to Material Preview had no effect and was rejected; the take shows Solid shading.

The director (Claude) injected one wrong edit on purpose (props-agent-90); it was rejected and rewound at 8:31, and the director's fallback marker then verified. It counts in the totals above and stays in the final scene.
The three renders were made afterwards by the director (Claude) from the agents' final scene, without geometry changes.
pieces.per_agent_note: * props includes the director's injected test (props-agent-90).

pieces.title: ViewPoint logo in 3D
pieces.subtitle: Four agents, microtask mode
pieces.blurb: The project's own mark, a lattice pylon with a clock motif, measured from the 2D logo (1000 px = 10 m) by a design agent and built in 3D by four agents taking turns.

facts.label: broker events verified
facts.source: TAKE_README.md · 16 STATE_VERIFIED + 6 VERIFIED; includes the director's injected test

honest: The director (Claude) injected one wrong edit on purpose (a 12 m slab, tower moved 5 m up); it was rejected and rewound at 3:02. It counts in the totals above; the director's marker is excluded from the .glb and hidden in the renders.
Two agents ran helper scripts from the CLI's default scratch folder and listed a folder inside the CLI's own configuration directory. The take notes report that no credential or token file was read.
The .glb export, hero renders and turntable were made after the take by the director (Claude), without geometry changes.
